task_instance: In a freshly created Expo (blank template) app, install expo-updates, then run `eas update:configure` to wire up EAS Update (channels, runtime version, updates.url) and attempt `eas update --channel preview --message "test"` to publish an OTA update.
blocker_detail: eas-cli's `update:configure` (and by extension `eas update`) requires an authenticated Expo/EAS account: running `npx eas-cli@latest update:configure --non-interactive` fails with 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable'. EAS Update is a paid/account-bound cloud service (project must be linked to an expo.dev account) and per the sandbox safety rules I cannot create/use an EAS account, log in, or supply an EXPO_TOKEN credential. This matches the skill document's own guidance: 'If the command cannot proceed because the project is not linked or the user has not authorized the required remote operation, stop after any independently valid package installation and explain what remains.' I completed the independently-valid local steps (scaffolding the app and installing expo-updates) and stopped there.
tools_used: Bash (npx create-expo-app, npm install, npx eas-cli@latest)
evidence: 1) Scaffolded project: `npx --yes create-expo-app@latest . --template blank` succeeded in /tmp/.../sample-app (464 packages installed). 2) `npx expo install expo-updates` failed only because it also calls an external React Native Directory compatibility API blocked by the sandbox proxy ('HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden'), so I installed the package directly with `npm install expo-updates`, which succeeded (8 packages added) and expo-updates now appears in node_modules/package.json. 3) `npx eas-cli@latest --version` -> 'eas-cli/24.8.0 linux-x64 node-v22.22.2', confirming the CLI itself runs fine in this runtime and network access to npm/eas-cli download works. 4) `npx eas-cli@latest update --help` printed full command help (update:configure, update:list, rollout flags, etc.), showing the tool is fully functional. 5) `npx eas-cli@latest update:configure --non-interactive` failed with: 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable ... Error: update:configure command failed.' This is the actual core deliverable of the skill (linking the project to EAS and configuring OTA updates) and it cannot proceed without an authenticated, account-bound Expo/EAS session, which the sandbox rules forbid me from creating or using.
